news.title: MSFT and META both expected to report on 28 Oct - neither date confirmed
news.body: Earnings calendars estimate Wednesday 28 Oct for both Microsoft and Meta, based on past schedules; neither company has confirmed. Both names sit in the MAG7 theme, so a shared report day is one event for the theme: a -10% gap in both costs $17,631 against a $6,000 theme cap, and stops do not protect through a scheduled report.
news.src: MarketBeat, Wall Street Horizon earnings calendars - Oct 2026 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/META/earnings/, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MSFT/earnings/)

news.title: EIA: 64 Bcf injection; surplus to the five-year average narrows
news.body: For the week to 25 Sep the EIA reported a 64 Bcf net injection. Working gas reached 3,415 Bcf: 79 Bcf (2.4%) above the five-year average, down from 95 Bcf a week earlier, and 138 Bcf (3.9%) below a year ago. Next report: Thu 8 Oct.
news.src: EIA Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report, released 1 Oct 2026 (https://ir.eia.gov/ngs/ngs.html)

news.title: SOXL +6.5% on 2 Oct; no single catalyst confirmed
news.body: SOXL closed at 163.71 on 2 Oct, up 6.5% from 153.69, 6.3% above the 154.00 entry. No company or sector announcement explaining the day's move was confirmed in the sources checked. SOXL resets its 3x leverage daily, so over several days its move can differ materially from 3x the index.

notes: NAV is $300,000 throughout - the notional mandate assigned by the firm. Never measured against account equity, by instruction. 1% = $3,000.
Limits are provisional, set 15 Sep 2026: 2% maximum loss per theme, 6% across the portfolio. Not a written company risk policy.
Themes are assigned, not fed. IBKR returns no sector tags; every theme in this file is a stated assumption.

Stop distances are shown as probability of being touched over a holding period, not in daily sigma - these are GTC orders with no expiry. The probability is the reflection-principle first-passage estimate 2*Phi(-ln(S/B)/(sigma*sqrt(T))) on realised daily vol, zero drift.

Stops are the account's GTC working orders, read through the IBKR connector when the board is refreshed in session; the unattended daily run carries the last read forward, because an IBKR Activity Flex Query cannot report working orders. Where a position has more than one stop, the nearest one drives the touch probabilities and the dollar risk sums every tranche. Still unconfirmed: whether they are enabled outside regular trading hours - most gaps occur overnight, which is exactly when a stop is least likely to help.

Scenario betas: UNG ~1.0 to front-month gas; MSFT and META 1.0 to mega-cap tech; SOXL 3.0 to the SOX (60-bar, corr 0.996 - its daily-reset leverage). Broad-market betas are 60-bar OLS on SPX: META 1.38, MSFT 1.88, SOXL 7.75. MSFT's is inflated by its 30 Jul earnings day (1.14 without it) and META's by its +11.3% day on 21 Sep (0.90 without it). UNG's market beta is negative (-0.51) and no hedge credit is taken for it. In the broad-market row MSFT breaches its stop only on the 60-bar beta (-5.6% vs a stop 5.1% below); at its 252-bar beta (0.99) or ex-outlier beta (1.14) it would not, and that row's clean loss would be $1.8k-$2.2k lower.

Scenario, slippage and gap figures are authored at the prices in price_basis (2 Oct IBKR regular-hours closes) against the positions in basis_book and do not move with the market. The tab flags them when prices drift past tolerance or the book changes.

The MAG7 theme is over its cap on stops alone: MSFT $5,306 + META $1,508 = $6,814 of stop risk against the $6,000 theme limit (114%). That is the limit set on 15 Sep, measured as written; resolving it is the account owner's call, not the board's.

Stops do not protect through a scheduled report. MSFT and META are both estimated to report on 28 Oct (unconfirmed). MSFT's 30 Jul report moved it 15.5% in a day; a -10% gap in both names would cost $17,631, 294% of the theme cap. The gap rows use the -10% scenario, so they are not the worst case.

SOXL is a 3x daily-leveraged fund. The -30% semiconductor row is a one-day shock; over several sessions daily rebalancing makes its path diverge from 3x the index, usually against the holder in a choppy market. Its 129 stop is 21.2% below the mark - about a 7% fall in the SOX.

Rates +50bp is not modelled for the book: on 3-year daily regressions on ^TNX (n=756) every holding's slope is positive (MSFT +0.020%/bp, t 1.79; SOXL +0.019, t 0.39; UNG +0.019, t 0.78; META +0.009, t 0.58) and none is significant. The excluded TLT (900 shares) is the rate exposure in this account - it falls when yields rise.
Independently reviewed. The first issue (15 Sep 2026) was blocked and reissued; the 27 Sep and 3 Oct re-derivations were each reviewed the same way before publishing.

Stopped out: GOOGL and GNRC on 23 Sep, SMCI on 24 Sep, CRM on 25 Sep, SNOW on 28 Sep 2026 (stop order filled 60 @ 319.43 and 40 @ 319.25 against a 328 stop, -$2,511.88 realised) and UNG's upper 1,500-share tranche the same day (10.65 / 10.655). Opened: SOXL 120 @ 154.00 on 1 Oct and META 100 (60 @ 740.59, 40 @ 740.90) on 2 Oct, both via buy stop-limit entries with the protective stops staged in advance - hence stop orders timestamped before the fills. Source: IBKR trade blotter (get_account_trades, 7 days) read 3 Oct. Themes for META (MAG7) and SOXL (Semiconductors) are assigned assumptions, not fed.

Parametric VaR sits above this window's history: the historical 5th percentile loss is $5,028 against a parametric 95% figure of $6,561, because the volatility estimate includes large up-days. That is a sample property, not safety - 60 days is a short tail sample. The worst day for today's holdings in the window was $6,712 on 2026-09-28, 0.72x the 99% VaR.

One day drives the 60-bar statistics for MSFT: MSFT +15.5% on 2026-07-30 (daily vol 2.53%, 1.61% without it; rolls off about 2026-10-23). Vol, beta, VaR and touch odds all fall when it leaves the window - a lower reading then is the window rolling, not risk falling, and it can land just before the next report.

Pairwise correlations over the window: META-MSFT -0.06; META-SOXL +0.08; META-UNG -0.14; MSFT-SOXL +0.21; MSFT-UNG -0.11; SOXL-UNG -0.07. With 60 observations each carries a standard error near 0.13, so treat any value inside about +/-0.26 as indistinguishable from zero, and a negative one as no dependable hedge. Taking no credit for the negative ones lifts 99% VaR from $9,277 to $9,681.
